title: EASM lookalike domains: the raw-domain key, deception methods, risk categories and missing signals

prose.text: Lookalike domains are registrations that imitate an organization's seed domains.

prose.label: Details call.
prose.text: The SDK may not read the details response correctly {{divergence:details-envelope}}.

prose.label: What a record does not say.
Trust.
prose.text: The registrant and hostname strings are authored outside the tenant, which is why the MCP tools flag them as untrusted: [[shared.mcp-server.results:untrusted-set]].

checks.do: For a lookalike details call returning empty fields, whether the raw body nests the record under results.
Whether hosting or MX evidence was gathered outside EASM before calling a lookalike active.

keyed-by-raw.statement: A lookalike domain is fetched by its raw domain name, not an opaque ID: `get_lookalike_domain` takes `lookalike_raw` and calls `/lookalike-domains/{lookalike_raw}/details`.

quotes: def get_lookalike_domain(self, org_id: str, lookalike_raw: str) -> APIResult[LookalikeDomainDetails]:

raw-and-original.statement: `lookalike_raw` is the lookalike domain and `original_domain` the legitimate domain it mimics.

expect.description: The legitimate domain mimicked by the lookalike domain

deception-methods.statement: `deception_method` is a list drawn from EdgeInsertion, Extension, Homograph, Hyphenation, KeyboardTypos, MidInsertion, Omission, PhoneticReplacement, Repetition, TldSwap, Typoglycemia, VowelReplacement and Typos.

risk-category.statement: `risk_category` is Phishing Lookalike, Registered Lookalike, Preventative Lookalike or Watchlist Lookalike, and `risk_score` is an integer.

status.statement: A lookalike entry's `status` is NOT_VERIFIED, VERIFIED, RISK_ACCEPTED, RESOLVED or DISPUTED.

registration.statement: `is_registered` says whether the domain is registered; `registrar`, `registered_by` and `expiration_date` are filled when available, and `created_date` is when EASM detected the domain.

expect.description: An individual or entity that owns the registered domain, if available.
The timestamp when the lookalike domain was detected in a scan and added to EASM
The internet company that was used to register the domain, if available.
The domain registration expiration date, if available.

no-hosting-signals.statement: A lookalike record has no similarity score, active-hosting or DNS/MX field.

remediation.description: Risk remediation recommendations for the lookalike domain

no-hosting-signals.conditions: The expect_absent names are the plausible spellings checked; the model's request format, quoted to its closing brace, lists fourteen fields and none of them.

skill-asks-for-signals.statement: The MCP server's EASM review skill asks the agent to report whether a lookalike domain actively hosts content and has MX records, with a similarity column in its example table.

quotes: - Whether the domain is actively hosting content
- DNS records (MX records suggest email phishing)
| Domain              | Similarity | Registered | Active | MX Records | Risk  |

signals-not-in-api.statement: The similarity, active-hosting and MX signals the skill asks for cannot come from the EASM API or the MCP tools; reporting them needs another source such as a DNS lookup.

details-envelope.summary: The contract wraps the lookalike details response in `results` and `total_results`; the SDK reads the details fields from the top level of the body.

positions.says: The details response has `results` (a list of lookalike records) and `total_results`.
`get_lookalike_domain` builds `LookalikeDomainDetails` directly from the response body.

details-envelope.impact: If the server follows the contract, the SDK's details object (and the MCP get tool) comes back with every field empty; read the raw body's results[0] instead.
